_meta.provenance: REPRESENTATIVE, NOT AUTHORITATIVE. Course codes, titles, credits, prerequisites and descriptions were written by hand to resemble a real Farmingdale State College catalog so the directory pages demo convincingly. They were NOT scraped from or verified against the official catalog, and some will be wrong. Replace this file with real catalog data via the import tool before anything is shown as fact.
_meta.ratings: Generated from a fixed random seed so this file is stable and reviewable in git.
_meta.professors_moved: Professors are NOT seeded here any more. Real faculty come from the official campus directory via `manage.py import_directory`. The fictional professors this file used to carry were removed once real, named people were in the database — invented ratings must never sit next to real names.
_meta.course_professor_links: Courses are no longer linked to professors. The directory says who works here, not who teaches what, and asserting that a real person teaches a course we cannot verify would be a fabrication. Links return when real schedule/catalog data does.

courses.title: Introduction to Programming
courses.description: A first programming course. Variables, control flow, functions, arrays, and basic problem decomposition, taught in Python with weekly lab work.

courses.title: Computer Programming II
courses.description: Object-oriented programming, recursion, file I/O, and an introduction to algorithm analysis. Continues the Python sequence and introduces Java.

courses.title: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Logic, proof techniques, sets, relations, functions, combinatorics, and graphs, with an emphasis on the mathematics used in later computing courses.

courses.title: Data Structures
courses.description: Lists, stacks, queues, trees, hash tables, and graphs. Implementation, asymptotic analysis, and the tradeoffs that decide which structure fits a problem.

courses.title: Computer Organization
courses.description: Number representation, digital logic, assembly language, the memory hierarchy, and how a high-level program actually executes on hardware.

courses.title: Database Management Systems
courses.description: Relational modeling, normalization, SQL, transactions, and indexing, with a term project building an application against a live database.

courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.description: Processes, threads, scheduling, synchronization, deadlock, memory management, and file systems, with programming assignments in C.

courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.description: Requirements, design, version control, testing, and code review, practiced on a semester-long team project.

courses.title: Web Application Development
courses.description: Server-side frameworks, templating, HTTP, authentication, and deployment. Students build and deploy a database-backed web application.

courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.description: Layered network architecture, TCP/IP, routing, reliability, and network programming with sockets.

courses.title: College Algebra
courses.description: Linear and quadratic equations, inequalities, functions and their graphs, exponentials and logarithms. Prepares students for precalculus.

courses.title: Precalculus
courses.description: Polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions, with the algebraic fluency calculus assumes.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: Limits, continuity, derivatives, and their applications, closing with the definite integral and the Fundamental Theorem.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: Techniques and applications of integration, sequences and series, parametric equations, and polar coordinates.

courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.description: Systems of linear equations, matrices, determinants, vector spaces, eigenvalues, and linear transformations.

courses.title: Calculus III
courses.description: Vectors, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector calculus through Green's and Stokes' theorems.

courses.title: Differential Equations
courses.description: First and second order equations, Laplace transforms, series solutions, and systems, with applications to physical models.

courses.title: Introduction to Statistics
courses.description: Descriptive statistics, probability, distributions, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and regression, using statistical software.

courses.title: Composition I
courses.description: Academic writing: developing a thesis, structuring an argument, integrating sources, and revising. Required of all students.

courses.title: Composition II: Writing About Literature
courses.description: Close reading and argument built from fiction, poetry, and drama, with a documented research essay.

courses.title: Technical Writing
courses.description: Documentation, reports, proposals, and instructions written for professional audiences, with attention to clarity and design.

courses.title: Introduction to Creative Writing
courses.description: Workshop in fiction and poetry. Students write, revise, and critique in a peer workshop setting.

courses.title: American Literature I
courses.description: American writing from the colonial period through the Civil War, read in historical context.

courses.title: Shakespeare
courses.description: A selection of comedies, histories, and tragedies, with attention to language, staging, and performance history.

courses.title: Introduction to Film Studies
courses.description: Film form, narrative, genre, and criticism, with weekly screenings and analytical writing.

courses.title: Advanced Composition
courses.description: Extended nonfiction projects with substantial revision, aimed at students who already write competently.

courses.title: Introduction to Business
courses.description: A survey of business functions: management, marketing, finance, accounting, and operations, and how they fit together in a firm.

courses.title: Financial Accounting
courses.description: The accounting cycle, financial statements, and the principles behind how transactions are recorded and reported to outsiders.

courses.title: Managerial Accounting
courses.description: Cost behavior, budgeting, variance analysis, and the accounting information managers use to make internal decisions.

courses.title: Principles of Marketing
courses.description: Segmentation, positioning, product, pricing, promotion, and distribution, applied through cases and a marketing plan.

courses.title: Business Law I
courses.description: Contracts, torts, agency, and the legal environment in which businesses operate, taught through case analysis.

courses.title: Principles of Management
courses.description: Planning, organizing, leading, and controlling, with attention to organizational structure and decision making.

courses.title: Corporate Finance
courses.description: Time value of money, valuation, capital budgeting, risk and return, and capital structure.

courses.title: Organizational Behavior
courses.description: Motivation, teams, leadership, communication, and culture, grounded in behavioral research.

courses.title: General Biology I
courses.description: Cell structure, metabolism, genetics, and evolution, with a laboratory. The first course for biology majors.

courses.title: General Biology II
courses.description: Diversity of life, plant and animal form and function, and ecology, with a laboratory.

courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology I
courses.description: Structure and function of the integumentary, skeletal, muscular, and nervous systems, with cadaver-model laboratory work.

courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology II
courses.description: Cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, urinary, endocrine, and reproductive systems, with laboratory.

courses.title: Microbiology
courses.description: Bacteria, viruses, and fungi; growth, control, and pathogenesis, with aseptic technique in the laboratory.

courses.title: Genetics
courses.description: Mendelian and molecular genetics, gene expression, and genomics, with problem sets and laboratory work.

courses.title: Cell Biology
courses.description: Membranes, organelles, the cytoskeleton, signaling, and the cell cycle, read partly through primary literature.

courses.title: Ecology
courses.description: Populations, communities, and ecosystems, with field work on and near campus.

courses.title: Introduction to Psychology
courses.description: A survey of the field: biological bases of behavior, learning, memory, development, personality, and psychological disorders.

courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Physical, cognitive, and social development across the lifespan, from infancy through late adulthood.

courses.title: Abnormal Psychology
courses.description: Classification, etiology, and treatment of psychological disorders, with attention to the limits of diagnosis.

courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: Attitudes, conformity, group behavior, persuasion, and attribution, grounded in classic and modern experiments.

courses.title: Research Methods in Psychology
courses.description: Experimental design, measurement, ethics, and statistical analysis, with students running and reporting their own study.

courses.title: Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: Attention, memory, language, reasoning, and decision making, read partly through primary literature.

courses.title: Health Psychology
courses.description: Behavioral factors in health and illness, stress and coping, and the design of health interventions.

courses.title: Psychology of Personality
courses.description: Major theories of personality and the evidence for and against them, including trait, psychodynamic, and social-cognitive accounts.

courses.title: Western Civilization I
courses.description: The ancient Near East through the Reformation, read through primary sources alongside a narrative text.

courses.title: Western Civilization II
courses.description: The Enlightenment to the present: revolution, industrialization, empire, and the world wars.

courses.title: American History I
courses.description: Colonization through Reconstruction, with attention to slavery, expansion, and the origins of the Civil War.

courses.title: American History II
courses.description: Reconstruction to the present: industrialization, immigration, the world wars, civil rights, and the postwar order.

courses.title: History of New York
courses.description: New York from Dutch settlement to the present, with a research project using local and digitized archives.

courses.title: Modern Europe
courses.description: Europe since 1789: nationalism, total war, fascism, the Cold War, and integration.

courses.title: History of Technology
courses.description: How technologies emerge and reshape work and society, from the steam engine through computing.

courses.title: The Civil War Era
courses.description: Sectional crisis, war, and Reconstruction, with substantial reading in primary documents.

courses.title: Architectural Design I
courses.description: Studio introduction to design: form, space, order, and representation, through a sequence of abstract and site-based projects.

courses.title: Architectural Design II
courses.description: Studio continuation with small buildings, program, and site, developing drawing and model-making skills.

courses.title: Architectural Graphics
courses.description: Orthographic projection, axonometrics, perspective, and freehand drawing, moving from hand drafting into CAD.

courses.title: Building Construction I
courses.description: Wood and light-gauge steel construction: assemblies, detailing, and the relationship between material and method.

courses.title: History of Architecture I
courses.description: Antiquity through the Renaissance, examined through buildings, cities, and the ideas that shaped them.

courses.title: Structures I
courses.description: Statics, loads, and the behavior of beams and columns, developing intuition for how buildings stand up.

courses.title: Environmental Systems
courses.description: Daylighting, thermal comfort, mechanical systems, and energy performance in building design.

courses.title: Digital Fabrication
courses.description: Parametric modeling and CNC, laser cutting, and 3D printing, applied to design prototypes.
